chunks: And from him, from Al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, who said: I asked a virtuous servant (peace be upon him) if it is permissible to recite two or three Surahs in the Night Prayer, and he said: 'Whatever is of the Night Prayer, recite two or three (Surahs), and whatever is of the Day Prayer, do not recite except one Surah at a time.'

key_terms.عَبْدٌ صَالِحٌ: A virtuous servant (referring to an Imam or learned figure)

ai.seo_question: What is the difference in recitation between the Night Prayer and Day Prayer according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This narration from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* highlights the jurisprudential flexibility in recitation volume, distinguishing the extended devotion of the Night Prayer (Salat al-Layl) from the more concise Day Prayer (Salat al-Nahar). It reflects the scholarly view that while multiple Surahs are permissible in the night, the day prayer emphasizes brevity and efficiency, often reciting one Surah per rak'ah to maintain focus and ease for the worshipper.
